question:
A monochromatic beam of wavelength $\lambda=500\,\text{nm}$ passes through a circular aperture of diameter $D=2\,\text{mm}$ and falls on a screen placed at distance $L=10\,\text{m}$.

A student claims: “Ray optics is a valid approximation up to $10\,\text{m}$, so diffraction spreading can be neglected.”

(i) Estimate the angular radius $\theta$ of the central diffraction maximum (first minimum) using the standard circular-aperture result.

(ii) Estimate the diameter of the central bright spot on the screen.

(iii) Using your estimate, decide whether the student’s claim is valid or invalid, and justify your conclusion quantitatively.

options.A: Claim is Valid. The central bright spot diameter is $\approx 0.61\,\text{mm}$, so spreading is negligible.
options.B: Claim is Invalid. The central bright spot diameter is $\approx 6.1\,\text{mm}$, which is not negligible compared to a $2\,\text{mm}$ aperture.
options.C: Claim is Valid. The central bright spot diameter is $\approx 0.061\,\text{mm}$, so ray optics is sufficient.
options.D: Claim is Invalid. Diffraction cannot occur for visible light passing through millimetre apertures.
